channel.title: The Bridge India - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from The Bridge India (thebridge.in)

item.title: CBI files FIR against Athlete Sachin Poswal for allegedly forging IDs to bypass doping ban
item.description: The Central Bureau of Investigation has accused Sachin Poswal of creating multiple fake athlete identities to compete despite a four-year doping suspension.

item.title: Alisha Choudhary becomes the first Indian Woman to win medal at Karate 1 Series
item.description: Alisha Choudhary became the first Indian woman to medal at a Karate 1 Series A event, winning bronze in the Women’s Kumite -55 kg category.

item.title: IOA reactivates National Olympic Academy in Ahmedabad, names PT Usha as President
item.description: The Indian Olympic Association has relaunched the National Olympic Academy with a renewed focus on athlete education and Olympic values.

item.title: Indian shuttlers target elusive first-ever title at India Open Super 750 - Preview
item.description: Indian shuttlers have not won a title at the India Open since the tournament was upgraded to BWF Super 750 status in 2023.

item.title: HS Prannoy's strategy for handling injury setbacks to extend his time at the top
item.description: The World Championship bronze medallist opens up about injuries, longer recovery, and still staying competitive at 33.

item.title: IWL 2025–26 phase 1 wrap: East Bengal flawless as title race takes shape
item.description: East Bengal dominate IWL Phase 1 as goals, clean sheets and Golden Boot race shape the 2025–26 Indian Women’s League title battle.

item.title: India Women set for three Türkiye friendlies ahead of AFC Asian Cup 2026
item.description: The Blue Tigresses will play three closed-door matches in Türkiye as part of their preparations for the AFC Women’s Asian Cup 2026.

item.title: SG Pipers open account; HIL GC go top after Kane Russell hat-trick in Men’s HIL
item.description: SG Pipers registered their first win of the season while HIL GC surged to the top of the table after victories in Ranchi.

item.title: Hyderabad to host Women’s 2026 FIH Hockey World Cup qualifiers
item.description: Eight nations will compete in Hyderabad in March 2026 for three spots at the Women’s FIH Hockey World Cup in Belgium and the Netherlands.

item.title: Harris–Mandhana blitz powers RCB to dominant nine-wicket win over UP Warriorz
item.description: A 137-run opening stand helped Royal Challengers Bengaluru chase down 144 in just 12.1 overs for their second straight WPL victory.
